# What does this PR do?

Lets users resume training from pre-0.14 distributed checkpoints that contain a serialized Adam, AdamW, or SGD optimizer.

For example, loading a legacy AdamW checkpoint with PyTorch 2.6 previously raised an `UnpicklingError` for `torch.optim.adamw.AdamW`. This change allows that optimizer to load through the existing weights-only loader. It registers the three optimizer classes and the `defaultdict(dict)` container used by their state. Checkpoints still use `weights_only=True`, and the existing test for rejecting an unregistered class continues to pass.

## Issue tracking

Linked issue: Fixes #1884

## Contribution process

### Pre-checks

- [x] I have added relevant unit tests
- [ ] I have added relevant functional tests
- [ ] If this PR adds or changes a GPU kernel (Triton, `jit_fuser`/`torch.compile`, CUDA extension, TE or external-library dispatch, or a scatter/index accumulation), I have added or updated its bit-exact determinism test and registered it in `tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/manifest.py` ([guide](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/docs/developer/determinism/testing.md))
- [ ] I have added proper typing to my code [Typing guidelines](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html)
- [ ] I have added relevant documentation
- [x] I have run the [autoformatter.sh](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/tools/autoformat.sh) checks on my PR

The GPU kernel checklist item does not apply to this change.

## Validation

At `6fe83895df691cb83458952c2da77915e57a15ec`, [CI run 36853974046](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/actions/runs/36853974046) passed linting and the distributed checkpointing bucket, including `test_legacy_optimizer` for Adam, AdamW, and SGD and `test_unsafe_globals`.

Earlier local validation recorded in this PR:

- `python -m pytest -q --confcutdir=tests/unit_tests/dist_checkpointing tests/unit_tests/dist_checkpointing/test_safe_globals.py::TestSafeGlobals::test_legacy_adamw_optimizer`
- Commit hooks: Black, Pylint, and isort

That test has since been renamed and parameterized as `test_legacy_optimizer`. The October 7 local check parsed both changed Python files and passed `git diff --check`. PyTorch, pytest, and NVIDIA GPUs are unavailable on this host, so GPU tests and a full training resume were not run locally.

The full hosted suite remains failed: the transformer bucket reported CUDA graph capture and gradient failures, the GB200 bucket reported Transformer Engine `ep_dispatch` receive-size assertions, and the SSM job was cancelled. `Nemo_CICD_Test` failed. These failures need maintainer triage; no base reproduction was performed.

### Code review

`NVIDIA/core-adlr` approval is missing, and ericharper's request for further review remains open. The PR is non-draft and has no merge conflicts.

Hi @deepujain , thinking through it, when we allowlist the `dict` and `defaultdict`, it actually means we allowlist anything, does it bring any security concerns? Also, user can simply walk-around this by adding any class through `torch.serialization.add_safe_globals`.

Light review — the fix is correct and minimal. Both `dict` and `defaultdict` are genuinely needed (a pickled optimizer carries `self.state = defaultdict(dict)`, so both the container and its `default_factory` get emitted as `GLOBAL` opcodes, and neither is in torch's default weights-only allowlist). Two things:

**1. The same failure still exists for `torch.optim.Adam` and `torch.optim.SGD`.**

In the Torch-fallback path the optimizer class is not always `AdamW`:

- `megatron/core/optimizer/__init__.py:565` — `adam_cls = torch.optim.AdamW if config.decoupled_weight_decay else torch.optim.Adam`
- `megatron/core/optimizer/__init__.py:32` — `from torch.optim import SGD` (used when `config.optimizer == "sgd"`)

A pre-0.14 `common.pt` produced with `decoupled_weight_decay=False` or `--optimizer sgd` serializes those classes and hits the identical `UnpicklingError`. Since the container types are now allowlisted, covering them is one line each — suggest adding `torch.optim.Adam` and `torch.optim.SGD` next to the new `torch.optim.AdamW` entry in `SAFE_GLOBALS`, and asserting on them in the test (parametrize `test_legacy_adamw_optimizer` over the three classes).

**2. Add a rationale comment for the new container entries.**

Non-obvious entries in `SAFE_GLOBALS` currently carry an explanatory comment (see the one on `torch._C.Generator`). Without one, `dict`/`defaultdict` look redundant with torch's built-in container handling and are easy to "clean up" later, which would silently re-break legacy loads. Suggest a short comment above `dict` noting that `optimizer.state` is a `defaultdict(dict)`, so both the container and its `default_factory` must be allowlisted.

Nit: `load_common` is deprecated and logs a warning on every call, so the new test will emit it. Harmless, just noting it in case a future `-W error` run trips on it.

Thanks — I pushed `8c87a79b0`, which adds `Adam` and `SGD` coverage alongside `AdamW`, parameterizes the regression test across all three, and documents why `optimizer.state` requires `defaultdict(dict)`.

On the security question: allowlisting `dict` and `defaultdict` permits only those built-in container types; it does not permit an arbitrary class carried inside their serialized state. The weights-only unpickler still rejects any non-allowlisted global referenced by a checkpoint. `defaultdict` additionally needs its `default_factory`, which is constrained here to the allowlisted `dict`. Calling `torch.serialization.add_safe_globals` is an explicit application-level opt-in for a trusted checkpoint, outside this library's default trust boundary.

Local validation: `py_compile` and `git diff --check` passed. This checkout does not include PyTorch or pytest, so the parameterized regression test is left for the approved CI run.

@@ -4,6 +4,7 @@
 import pickle
 import threading
 from argparse import Namespace
+from collections import defaultdict
 from io import BytesIO
 from pathlib import PosixPath
 from signal import Signals
@@ -27,6 +28,10 @@
 )
 
 SAFE_GLOBALS = [
+    # Legacy optimizer checkpoints serialize optimizer.state as defaultdict(dict),
+    # requiring both the container and its default factory for weights-only loads.
+    dict,
+    defaultdict,
     SimpleNamespace,
     PosixPath,
     _reconstruct,
@@ -47,6 +52,9 @@
     # Allow frozenset values in legacy checkpoint metadata when loading with weights_only=True.
     frozenset,
     Signals,
+    torch.optim.Adam,
+    torch.optim.AdamW,
+    torch.optim.SGD,
     torch._C.Generator,  # Needed for torch ckpt format loading after weights_only default change
 ]

@@ -9,6 +9,7 @@
 import pytest
 import torch
 
+from megatron.core.dist_checkpointing.strategies.common import COMMON_STATE_FNAME, load_common
 from megatron.core.safe_globals import SafeUnpickler
 from megatron.core.utils import is_torch_min_version
 
@@ -33,6 +34,18 @@ def test_safe_globals(self, tmp_path_dist_ckpt):
 
         torch.load(ckpt_path)
 
+    @pytest.mark.skipif(not is_torch_min_version("2.6a0"), reason="PyTorch 2.6 is required")
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
+        "optimizer_cls", [torch.optim.Adam, torch.optim.AdamW, torch.optim.SGD]
+    )
+    def test_legacy_optimizer(self, tmp_path, optimizer_cls):
+        optimizer = optimizer_cls([torch.nn.Parameter(torch.ones(1))])
+        torch.save({"optimizer": optimizer}, tmp_path / COMMON_STATE_FNAME)
+
+        state_dict = load_common(tmp_path)
+
+        assert isinstance(state_dict["optimizer"], optimizer_cls)
+
     @pytest.mark.skipif(not is_torch_min_version("2.6a0"), reason="PyTorch 2.6 is required")
     def test_unsafe_globals(self, tmp_path_dist_ckpt):
